hosted_note: 0181_multi_studio_command_authority.sql APPLIED to production 2026-08-13, MIGRATION-FIRST, via `npx --yes supabase@2.102.0 db push --linked --yes` from a worktree checked out at the authorized #573 head 634a06a7c9a7d81eb1c78ae4fc6803af263215ac (project alhhybgqdmcdyzpybykj), raw sha256 2f5bcbd5854b1201835f6151debffa940e98035e6a4d88865da1d86fb3da195f. APPLY EXIT STATUS: PUSH EXIT CODE 0 WAS CAPTURED (the command was backgrounded specifically so a harness timeout could not obscure it, which is what happened on the 0180 apply). A DRY RUN immediately before proposed 0181 AND NOTHING ELSE. WHAT IT FIXES — P1 PRODUCTION INCIDENT: a practitioner with TWO active studio memberships could open /clients/<id>/sessions/new (HTTP 200) and receive HTTP 500 on selecting a modality, 'Failed to start session: Client not found in this studio.' (digest 2140849265). 0167's start_session resolved the acting studio with `where user_id = auth.uid() and active = true limit 1` — no studio input, no predicate, NO ORDER BY — so the page rendered against the SELECTED studio while the command ran against an ARBITRARY membership. 0181 adds an EXPLICIT p_studio_id (no DEFAULT) which is NOT trusted: an ACTIVE practitioner row for auth.uid() in that studio is re-proven at the SECURITY DEFINER boundary and the practitioner id is derived from that same row. SECOND DEFECT CLOSED IN THE SAME FILE: 0167 claimed 'FOR UPDATE closes the read-then-insert race'. That is false when the coalesce window is EMPTY — `for update` locks rows and an empty result set locks nothing — so two overlapping first taps could both insert. 0181 takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed on (studio, client, practitioner, modality) after authority is proven and before the lookup. ROLLOUT ORDER WAS MANDATORY AND WAS FOLLOWED: the four-argument signature is RETAINED as a thin delegating wrapper (studio derived from the CLIENT plus an active membership, no arbitrary pick), so OLD APP + NEW DB is safe; the database was applied FIRST and independently verified, the OLD application was confirmed healthy against the NEW database (hone.care / 200, /login 200, /portal/login 200, /pricing 200, /dashboard 307 to /login) BEFORE any merge, and only then was #573 merged. The application also carries a PGRST202 single-retry floor for the reverse skew (new app, rolled-back DB) so a rollback degrades to today's behaviour rather than a total outage. POST-APPLY VERIFICATION (read-only): hosted migration history max 0181 with version 0181 recorded EXACTLY ONCE and nothing above it (180 rows total); public.start_session present with EXACTLY TWO signatures; deployed 5-arg body md5 aeb2aaab97ce887739725ddd749dd355 length 6569, deployed 4-arg wrapper body md5 82a3c07bd53d48661089bb0454703902 length 1042; both prosecdef true with proconfig search_path=""; neither carries an argument DEFAULT; the 5-arg re-proves membership via session_actor_practitioner(v_studio_id), constrains the client to that studio, retains all three appointment lineage checks, holds the advisory lock AND the row-level FOR UPDATE; the 4-arg derives the studio from the client + an active membership, contains NO limit 1 and NO insert, and delegates; EXECUTE granted to authenticated ONLY on both signatures (acl postgres=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres — no PUBLIC, no anon, no service_role). LIVE-SCHEMA CENSUS: unsafe unconstrained auth.uid() practitioner LIMIT-1 resolvers = 0. The single unconstrained match, reconcile_my_pending_invitation, is a deterministic ORDER BY-ed read of the caller's own terms/privacy acceptance stamps in a path whose studio comes from the invitation resource — not an actor pick. PRE-APPLY DUPLICATE CENSUS (read-only, informational): 0 suspicious pairs across 167 live sessions sharing the full coalesce identity within the 90-minute window, so the empty-window race was possible but never fired in production. ZERO BUSINESS-ROW MUTATION: 0181 contains NO table DDL, NO index change, NO backfill and NO row mutation — its only statements are two CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION, the per-signature revoke/grant pairs and two COMMENT ON FUNCTION. POST-MERGE: #573 merged as a normal two-parent merge commit ac9c1c0f77439f201dcd432c188a5e7265b8d289 (parent 1 10426997bea765b02f3e66f1eadfcb849d964adb = previous production, parent 2 = the authorized head); branch protection unchanged and not bypassed; Vercel Production deployment dpl_9H5fTFTBUWBk2RXSGyGdgpYXY6QC built and Ready, and hone.care was PROVEN to route to it by matching live request logs. Post-deploy logs on the new deployment: ZERO 'Client not found in this studio', ZERO start_session_studio_aware_signature_missing (no PGRST202 fallback, which is the expected result of a correct migration-first order), zero error-level rows. READ-ONLY STRUCTURAL PROOF OF THE FIX: production holds exactly 2 users with 2+ active memberships (matching the two reported accounts); before 0181, 4 reachable clients per user failed the arbitrary pick (user 2 could reach NONE of its 4); after 0181 every reachable client passes the authority rule — 54/54 and 4/4, with 0 still broken. MANUAL PRODUCTION SMOKE: PASS — USER-PERFORMED. After this rollout, the previously failing multi-studio practitioner account was retested by hand in production: client profile -> Log session -> the previously failing modality/session-start path, with NO HTTP or application error observed. This is a MANUALLY REPORTED result from a real account, not synthetic automation and not server-side instrumentation: no session id, client id, precise timestamp or server trace is recorded here because none was captured, and none is invented. It is recorded as the human confirmation that the incident is closed on the account that originally reported it. The two proofs are deliberately kept distinct — the AUTOMATED/STRUCTURAL evidence above (live-schema verification plus the read-only membership/authority proof) was produced by measurement; this line is the MANUAL real-account confirmation. No production session was created BY THE ROLLOUT ITSELF; the session created during the manual retest was created by the practitioner in the ordinary course of using the product. FINAL STATE: repository max 0181, hosted max 0181, repo == hosted, nothing pending, next free 0182 (AVAILABLE BUT NOT CLAIMED).
